diagnostics.message: resource.aws_lambda_function.main does not depend on resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.main, but the CloudWatch log group for a Lambda function must exist before the function itself. Here the ordering is actually inverted: the log group's name references aws_lambda_function.main.function_name, so Terraform creates the function first. If the function is invoked before the log group is created, Lambda auto-creates a log group with default settings (no retention), and the subsequent aws_cloudwatch_log_group.main create fails with an "already exists" conflict. The provider docs explicitly recommend depends_on = [aws_cloudwatch_log_group...] on the function. Note the proper fix is to compute the log group name from a local (e.g. "/aws/lambda/${var.lambda.prefix}-${var.lambda.name}") to break the reverse reference, then add depends_on on the function — otherwise the two edges would form a cycle.

resource.aws_lambda_function.main references aws_iam_role.main.arn but has no dependency on resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.vpc_execution_role, which attaches the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole policy the function needs to manage network interfaces in its VPC config. When var.lambda.subnet_ids is non-empty, the function is created with VPC attachment before that permission is attached; the provider docs recommend depends_on from the lambda function to its role policy attachment to ensure execution permissions are in place (IAM propagation is eventually consistent).

resource.aws_lambda_function.main does not depend on resource.aws_iam_role_policy.xray, which grants the X-Ray permissions the function needs when var.lambda.tracing_config.mode is set. Since IAM policy propagation is eventually consistent, the function can exist (and start being invoked/tracing) before the xray-policy is attached and propagated; the provider docs' canonical Lambda logging/permissions example places the role's policy attachment in the function's depends_on for the same reason.
